instruction.text: Complete the statements about the geography of Oceania.

atoms.b: The continent of Oceania is made up of the large island country of Australia, New Zealand and many other smaller ((++islands seas)).
Around Oceania, you will find the ((++Indian Atlantic)) Ocean to the west and the Pacific Ocean to the east.
In the centre of Australia, there is a desert with a huge, red sandstone monolith called ((++Uluru Melbourne)).
The cities with the most people in Oceania are ((++Sydney Uluru)) and Melbourne in Australia.

instruction.text: The country of Australia is known for many things. Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Kangaroos are found almost exclusively in this country and can jump up to 13 metres.
The red sandstone monolith called Uluru is a landmark of Australia.
Before the first Europeans came to Australia, the Aboriginal peoples lived there. They take particularly good care of nature.
Large parts of Australia are uninhabited. After Antarctica, it has the lowest population density in the world.

instruction.text: Complete the statements about the geography of Antarctica.

atoms.b: The continent of Antarctica is home to the ((++South_Pole North_Pole)) and is mostly covered by ((++ice sand)).
This large, ice island is surrounded by the ((++Southern Atlantic)) Ocean.

instruction.text: Read the text about living conditions in Antarctica.

atoms.text: Unlike the other continents, no indigenous human inhabitants live in Antarctica. Apart from a few scientists and researchers, hardly any people live here.
Instead, Antarctica is home to seals, penguins and whales. The animals of Antarctica feed mainly on marine life because there are also very few plants here.

feedback.wrong: Polar bears do not live in Antarctica. They are only found in the far north of the Arctic, for example in Canada and Alaska.
